subject.title: fix(browser): bound Playwright response body reads to prevent OOM

question: Should browser `responsebody` omit known-length oversized bodies with `truncated: true`, or preserve a truncated prefix for compatibility?
rationale: The PR fixes a real memory hazard but changes the observable result shape for `content-length > maxBytes`, so automation should not choose the permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept omitted body after proof
options.body: Require current-head real proof for content-length pre-reject and CLI notice, then land the empty-body `truncated: true` contract.

options.title: Preserve prefix semantics
options.body: Remove the content-length early omit path and keep only the bounded decode mitigation if existing output shape matters more.

options.title: Hold for streaming design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers require truly bounded capture for unknown-length responses without Playwright full-buffer reads.

recommendation.title: Accept omitted body after proof
recommendation.body: Require current-head real proof for content-length pre-reject and CLI notice, then land the empty-body `truncated: true` contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest feature-history ownership for the browser responsebody helper and surrounding browser CLI behavior.
